name: Turnpike Troubadours
notes: The red-dirt centre of the archetype and its main non-Nashville chart presence: Oklahoma country-rock with a full-time fiddle and Cajun and bluegrass borrowings. `bpm` takes the entry's stated 100–175 straight-on-2&4 band. ⚠ `era` collapses the entry's two disjoint windows — "window 2010–2019 and 2022–present" — into one span. The entry states one lane, one lineup and one BPM band across both and names nothing that changes at the 2019–2022 gap, so no parameter here is windowed; the collapse is this author's reading, not a research statement. Drums are the entry's own comparative instruction: "a real kit is present at all times, which is what separates this entry from the bluegrass wing — model it as a rock-sized train beat: full backbeat, audible room, crash accents at section starts", plus "a straight 8th snare stream with sticks and a two-beat kick on the uptempo cuts, opening to quarter kick under choruses" and "the Cajun-adjacent cuts use a two-step feel with the hat opening on 4". So `velocityTiers.accent` is 110–127, `percs` carries a crash lane at −4 dB, `kick` is [2,4] on anchors 1 and 3, and `openHat.pos` is ["4"] at 0.32. The countermelody is the loudest single claim in the entry — "fiddle (Kyle Nix) is a permanent band member and the primary answering voice" and "the melodic interest carried by the fiddle line rather than the vocal" — so `densityRatio` is 0.75, the highest in this section's radio wing, against a plain, syllabically dense, low-ornament vocal in the melody block. Harmony is the stated I–IV–V and I–V–vi–IV with modal ♭VII from the fiddle plus the Cajun two-chord I–V vamp. The song form keeps the entry's "three verses more often than the Nashville two". ⚠ The entry states outright: "no per-track tempo or key readings were reachable" and "all tempo and harmonic numbers inferred" [LOW-CONF]. That flag applies to `bpm.mode` 140, to the key weights over the stated guitar keys G/D/A/E, and to every progression weight here. ⚠ Also INFERRED: velocity tiers, `percs` contents, humanize and the melody register and density.
